source: 911 call from Duxbury, Massachusetts, January 24, 2023. Transcript entered in Commonwealth v. Clancy. The audio was played for the jury in July 2026; the court did not release it publicly, so no real recording exists outside the case file.
_accuracy: Every 'text' below is word-for-word from the transcript except for expanded numerals and normalized capitalization, which change how a voice pronounces a line but not what it says. Direction lives in 'tag' and is never part of 'text', so the quoted words stay auditable. Two kinds of line carry skip:true - ones the transcript scrambles beyond safe attribution, and ones cut from this edit. The note on each says which.
_edit: This cut is the end of the call only: he tells the dispatcher he has to check on the kids, walks away with the line open, and she is left calling into the house. The earlier medical questions are kept below as skip:true so they can come back, but they play as ordinary conversation and were cut for it.
_direction: Tags are ElevenLabs v3 audio tags, prepended at render time. 'distance': 'away' means he has walked off with the phone live - quieter, duller, room reflections. A negative 'gap' starts a line before the previous one ends, so people talk over each other; that overlap is what stops it sounding like turn-taking.
